description: Execute an action against a service (AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, or GitHub) using Akeyless secret credentials (dynamic or rotated), or run a single non-interactive command on a remote host: a shell command over SSH (SSH targets and SSH certificate issuers) or a PowerShell/CMD command over WinRM (Windows and LDAP items). A remote command returns stdout, stderr, exit_code and cwd. Accepts natural language or CLI-style payloads for services (e.g. 'list all S3 buckets', 'kubectl get pods -n default', 'list open PRs') and a literal command line for remote hosts (e.g. 'uptime', 'Get-Service'). To choose the host, the working directory or the shell, or to upload or download a file, send a remote item a sub-tool call as the payload, e.g. {"tool":"run","arguments":{"command":"<command>","host":"<host>"}}; list-sub-tools returns the remote sub-tools and their arguments. Returns the results as JSON. Credentials are never exposed. IMPORTANT: Always ask the user for the secret name if it was not provided. Use the list-secrets tool to discover available secrets.

auth-code.description: OAuth authorization code returned after the user authorizes in the browser. Only required when the previous call returned an authorization URL.

original-prompt.description: The user's original natural-language request before the agent translated it into an action.

original-user.description: The human end-user behind the agent (for auditing).

payload.description: The action to execute. Can be natural language (e.g. 'list all S3 buckets') or CLI-style (e.g. 'aws s3 ls').

secret-name.description: Full path of the Akeyless secret — dynamic or rotated (e.g. /MyFolder/my-aws-ds).

state.description: OAuth state parameter returned with the authorization URL. Must be passed back together with auth-code.

name: service-execute
title: Execute Service Action
